name: Carlos Bianchi

spellsCounted.reason: Clausura 1993, Apertura 1995, Clausura 1996, Libertadores and Intercontinental 1994, Interamericana 1996. Start = first match on the bench (21 Feb 1993); Wikipedia says he returned in December 1992 and its table gives 1 July 1993, so the exact day he took charge is unconfirmed. End is Wikipedia's table date (1996-06-30), single source.
Apertura 1998, Clausura 1999, Apertura 2000, Libertadores 2000 and 2001, Intercontinental 2000, 40-match unbeaten record. Dates from Wikipedia's table only (single source).
Apertura 2003, Libertadores 2003, Intercontinental 2003. Start per Wikipedia table (1 Jan 2003); Página/12 (2002-12-22) says he would start 6 January 2003. End per Wikipedia table, single source.

spellsExcluded.reason: 31 matches (12W 9D 10L, Wikipedia), no titles, dismissed; no tactical coverage found. Short, failed.
21 matches (6W 8D 7L), no titles, dismissed; no tactical coverage found.
Third spell: no major titles, sacked; no sources mined; 2013 snippets (4-4-1-1 with Riquelme) not verified; outside the period that made him known.
Second division and relegation-battle spells with no titles; digest says methods there were 'geared towards discipline and aggression' but they are pre-fame.

scopeNote: Counted: Vélez 1993-96 and Boca 1998-2001 and 2003-04, the spells behind his record of four Libertadores titles. Style per sources: a 4-3-1-2 with Riquelme as enganche (El Gráfico/La Nación/Télam), 'nobody changes a formula that gives results', pragmatic and system-adaptive ('Los sistemas siempre los definí en función a los jugadores'); Vélez could go to a 5-3-2 away (1994 final). Partial dates in spellsExcluded (2013-01, 2014, 1985-03, 1992) are used because exact days were not researched for excluded spells. Dates are partial or single-source: Wikipedia's table gives 1 July 1993 for the Vélez start while the text says he took over in December 1992 (first match 1993-02-21). The popular 'Virrey' label comes from Vélez. No source mined states zonal vs man-marking as policy; the only marking evidence is a personal marker on Figo in the 2000 Intercontinental plus an offside trap. Evidence for the 2003-04 spell is thin (mostly retrospectives of the 2003 titles); the pressing and transitions evidence is a single 2001 match report.
openQuestions: Exact start day at Vélez (December 1992 appointment vs 21 Feb 1993 first match vs 1 July 1993 in Wikipedia table) and exact end days of all spells (Wikipedia table only).

Zonal vs man-marking policy not found: only evidence is Matellán's personal marking of Figo (2000-11-28) and an offside trap; defensive scheme at Vélez 1993-96 unconfirmed beyond the 5-3-2 away at the 1994 final.
Boca's formation is described as 4-3-1-2 (Télam, La Nación) but as 4-4-1-1 in a Goal retrospective of the 2001 Palmeiras match: contested label.
Boca 2013-14 spell was excluded without mining; reconsider if the app needs a late-career profile.
Little 2003-04 tactical coverage; the 2003 Boca (Tevez) and the 3-4-3 mentioned in a search summary against Vélez (ESPN page unreadable) were not verified.

sources.title: Bianchi no cambiará los actuales sistemas de juego (Télam)
sources.evidence: Boca habitualmente dispone a sus hombres en el campo de juego con un esquema de 4-3-1-2, y en ese sentido, Bianchi reiteró en varias ocasiones que “nadie cambia una fórmula que da resultados”.

sources.title: La primera Copa Libertadores de Bianchi en Boca (La Nación)
sources.evidence: Boca jugaba 4-3-1-2. "¿Y la Juventus de Zidane cómo jugaba?", comparaba con el equipo italiano por esos tiempos Bianchi porque muchos veían lo moderno en los espejos europeos.

sources.title: El partido más riquelmeano de Román (Goal)
sources.evidence: 4-4-1-1. Bianchi no salió a especular, porque los primeros 35 minutos fueron casi todos de Boca, pero no regaló ni un espacio.

sources.title: O clube de bairro que se fez do tamanho do mundo (Trivela)
sources.evidence: Sem Sotomayor no miolo de zaga, Bianchi preferiu escalar o Vélez num 5-3-2, protegendo mais a defesa com as entradas de Héctor Almandoz e Mauricio Pellegrino.

sources.title: Carlos Bianchi: pasado de copas (El Gráfico, interview with Fox Sports)
sources.evidence: Cuando vi sus características, no tuve dudas: para mí, era el 10 ideal, ese jugador que podía hacer jugar a los dos de adelante, a los marcadores de punta o a un volante llegando por sorpresa.

sources.title: The bold brilliance of Carlos Bianchi (These Football Times)
sources.evidence: Setting Riquelme free in the number 10 position and allowing him to stay up-field and drift into space, the mercurial midfielder repaid the faith by helping Boca lift three domestic titles in 1998, 1999 and 2000.

sources.title: A forensic analysis of Riquelme's magnum opus v Real Madrid (Planet Football)
sources.evidence: Riquelme was in the groove, fully aware of what was required to keep his side in the lead. He was not a great one for defending, but if you can keep the ball in the opposition half, push them back and draw fouls, then you do not need to.

sources.title: Página/12 (Boca 3-0 Vasco, Libertadores)
sources.evidence: el equipo de Bianchi se plantó muy adelante, ejerció profunda presión sobre el mediocampo rival y en sólo un minuto creó tres situaciones de gol.

sources.title: A forensic analysis of Riquelme's magnum opus v Real Madrid (Planet Football)
sources.evidence: Unfortunately for them, the offside trap set by Bianchi was working perfectly. Twice Madrid put the ball into the Boca net in the second period, twice the assistant’s flag was raised.

sources.title: En el recuerdo: Boca Campeón Intercontinental 2000 (El Gráfico)
sources.evidence: sacó del equipo a Daniel Fagiani, que había sido titular durante todo el proceso previo, y en su lugar incluyó a Aníbal Matellán, que se encargaría de la marca personal de Figo.

sources.title: The bold brilliance of Carlos Bianchi (These Football Times)
sources.evidence: Everyone knew their roles in the finest detail, with Bianchi spending hours on the training ground perfecting their set-piece routines and defensive stability.
